3334.text: In 1Cor.13.5 the surface sense 'insist on its own way' diverges from the base gloss 'seek/look for' -- here it carries the specific nuance of self-assertive demanding rather than neutral searching, the negative pole of the seeking-characteristic, contrasting with Luke.2.48's compassionate, other-directed searching for a lost child.

3336.text: In 1Cor.13.5 'love' (personified as the party/subject) is described as NOT initiating self-seeking; the negated operation is directed toward 'its own way' -- i.e., love characteristically refrains from directing this seeking-operation toward its own interest at others' expense.

3338.text: In 1Cor.13.5 M02 (irritable), M26 (resentful), M58 (evil/resentful) co-occur; love's refusal to seek its own way (G2212, negated) stands alongside its refusal to be irritable or resentful -- these are parallel negated vices in Paul's list, each independently describing what love does NOT do, without one being derived from another.

3844.text: In Matt.12.39 epizēteō carries its established Gospel sense of demanding a sign; matches the term's consistent usage elsewhere (e.g. Luke.11.29), no additional divergence.

3845.text: In Luke.11.29 epizēteō repeats the identical idiom and sense found in Matt.12.39 (demanding a sign from 'this generation'), showing no divergence between occurrences.

3846.text: In Matt.12.39, epizēteō (seeks for) co-occurs with M58 (evil), M57 (adulterous), M43 (sign, x3), and M43 (prophet); the generation's evil/adulterous character (M58/M57) is what motivates and characterizes its demanding of a sign (M43) -- epizēteō is the operative verb connecting the moral characteristics to the demanded object, rather than being modified by them.

3847.text: In Luke.11.29, epizēteō (seeks for) co-occurs with M08 (began), M58 (evil), and M43 (sign, x3); as in Matt.12.39, the evil characterization of the generation supplies the moral cause of its sign-demanding act, with epizēteō serving as the link-verb between disposition and demanded object.

3848.text: In Matt.12.39, epizēteō is role-T3, initiated by 'an evil and adulterous generation' and directed at Jesus (the implicit addressee 'he answered them') demanding a sign.

3849.text: In Luke.11.29, epizēteō is role-T3, initiated by 'this generation' and directed at Jesus, demanding a sign as in the parallel Matt.12.39 saying.

4201.text: In 1Sam.16.16 ('seek out a man') and 1Sam.28.7 ('Seek out...a woman') and 2Sam.17.20 ('sought and could not find'), the surface sense of procurement/search sits squarely within the base gloss with no notable shift.

4203.text: In 1Sam.16.16, the seeking operation is initiated by the servants (at the lord's command) and directed toward finding 'a man skillful in playing the lyre' -- the party sought is the skilled musician, a benign procurement operation.

4209.text: In 1Sam.16.16, M36 (servants), M15 (skillful), M24/M58 (harmful), M47 (spirit), M05/M18 (well) all co-occur; baqash's own vantage is that the seeking-out act is the mechanism by which the household responds to Saul's affliction -- the procurement operation links the human agents to the remedy, distinct from the affliction/skill terms themselves.

4256.text: In 1Sam.16.16, 'harmful spirit from God' diverges from ruach's more common empowering/animating sense (e.g. Spirit of God imparting gifts) -- here the divergence is toward an afflicting, tormenting agency; the impact is to frame Saul's distress as divinely permitted affliction requiring music as remedy.

4270.text: In 1Sam.16.16 'harmful' sits within the base gloss's 'hurtful/evil' sense (1h), a standard, unremarkable application; no notable divergence.

4674.text: In Acts.10.19 and Acts.10.21, zeteo functions in its plain concrete sense 'looking for/seeking' -- the three men sent by Cornelius seeking Peter. This sits squarely within the base gloss with no distinguishing theological or hostile nuance, a straightforward physical search for a specific person.

4683.text: M47 (Spirit) is present in Acts.10.19 as the divine speaker announcing that men are seeking Peter; the Spirit's speech-act and the men's seeking are related narratively (the Spirit reveals the seeking) but the Spirit itself does not seek -- it discloses and directs, a distinct characteristic from the seeking it reports.

4684.text: M26 (reason/aitia, front-loaded) co-occurs with seeking in Acts.10.21 -- Peter confirms he is the one sought, then asks the reason (aitia) for the visitors' coming. The seeking (their prior action) prompts Peter's request for the reason behind it; reason-seeking here follows and explains the initial seeking rather than being enacted by it.

4693.text: In Acts.10.19 the seeking/looking-for operation is initiated by the three men (party, T8) sent by Cornelius and directed toward Peter ('you'), reported to Peter by the Spirit.

4694.text: In Acts.10.21 the seeking/looking-for operation is initiated by the men (party, T8) and directed toward Peter, who confirms himself as the one sought when he goes down to meet them.

4707.text: In Acts.10.21 aitia is used in its plain practical sense 'reason/cause' (for the men's coming) -- sitting within the base gloss with no notable divergence.

4733.text: In Acts.10.19 enthymeomai is used in its plain base sense 'ponder/consider carefully,' matching the tree's sole NT occurrence gloss with no additional divergence noted (this is its only NT occurrence, so no comparative pattern across multiple occurrences exists).

4770.text: In Acts.9.11 'look for' (imperative, seeking a specific named man) sits squarely within the base gloss of physical searching for a person; no divergent nuance from the general stepGloss.

4988.text: In Esth.2.2 'sought out' shifts H1245 toward administrative procurement/selection (gathering virgins for the king), a bureaucratic sense distinct from personal or religious seeking seen elsewhere -- the impact is depersonalized, institutional searching rather than individual pursuit.

4992.text: In Esth.2.2 the king's young men initiate the seeking-out operation directed toward beautiful young virgins, on behalf of the king.

4996.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs meaningfully with H1245 in Esth.2.2 as home-cluster interaction; the seeking-out operates alongside descriptive terms (beauty, youth) but no other M-code party characteristic is present.

5128.text: In Ezek.26.21 'sought for' is the Pual passive of H1245 ('to be sought'), used literally of Tyre no longer being found even if searched for -- this matches the base gloss's own passive sense (1b) exactly, no additional nuance.

5129.text: Here H1245 appears passively ('sought for') with no explicit human initiator named in this clause; the implied searchers are unnamed observers who would seek Tyre, directed toward the city itself, but she will not be found -- an operation of search rendered permanently frustrated.

5130.text: M01 (dreadful end/terror) is also present in this verse but describes Tyre's fate directly, distinct from the seeking-motif which describes the impossibility of ever locating her afterward; the two M-codes describe sequential rather than interacting aspects of judgment.

5166.text: In Prov.1.28 'seek me diligently' uses H7836 in its ordinary earnest-seeking sense (personified Wisdom as object); this sits squarely within the base gloss, though the futility (seeking too late, after refusing to listen earlier) is supplied by narrative context, not the verb's own shift.

5167.text: The seeking operation is initiated by 'they' (those who earlier refused wisdom's call) and directed toward personified Wisdom ('me'), paired with 'call upon me' and answered by refusal ('I will not answer') -- an operation of belated, futile pursuit.

5168.text: M42 (call) and M22 (answer) are also present, describing the paired invocation and refusal; H7836's diligent seeking supplies the futile intensified pursuit that follows the call, but the M-codes describe distinct acts (calling vs seeking) rather than one shaping the other's meaning.

5260.text: In Isa.62.12 'Sought Out' functions as a passive-participle EPITHET/name for the restored city rather than describing an act of seeking performed by the city -- a nominalized, identity-conferring nuance distinct from the active-seeking sense elsewhere; the impact is to make the city's new identity itself the proof that it is desired/valued rather than forsaken.

5265.text: In Isa.62.12, H1875 ('Sought Out') is tightly related to M61 (Holy) and M79 (Redeemed): together they form a triad of covenant-identity epithets for the restored city -- holy status, redeemed status, and sought-out status jointly constitute the new name replacing the old reproach; being 'sought out' specifically supplies the relational proof that the city is now wanted rather than abandoned.

5712.text: Isa.26.9's 'earnestly seeks' sits squarely within shachar's base intensive-devotional gloss -- no additional nuance beyond the term's characteristic sense.

5713.text: Isa.26.9 pairs shachar (earnestly seeking God) with M47 (soul/spirit, twice) and M12/M26 (judgments) and M12 (righteousness). From seeking's vantage: the intensive devotional seeking is the inward disposition (soul/spirit) that anticipates and responds to God's outward judgments producing righteousness in the world -- seeking here is the relational bridge between inward longing and the world's moral learning.

5753.text: In Isa.26.9 shachar ('earnestly seeks') is the operation, initiated by the speaker's own spirit (first-person), directed toward God (2ms 'you') -- an inward-to-divine directed act.

5848.text: In 1Chr.28.8 'seek out' the commandments matches the base covenantal-inquiry sense of the word without special divergence.

5852.text: In 1Chr.28.8, 'seek out' is initiated by Israel (addressed assembly, party) directed toward the commandments of the Lord God (party/object), an act of covenantal compliance.

5856.text: In 1Chr.28.8, H1875 (seeking) co-occurs with M44 (assembly) and M54 (commandments): seeking here is the covenantal act binding the assembled community to the given commandments -- the seeking-characteristic supplies the active verb that makes the community's relation to the commandments (M54) operative.

5964.text: In Matt.6.32 and Luke.12.30, 'seek(after)' carries the nuance of anxious, worry-driven pursuit of material necessities by the Gentiles/nations, contrasted with trusting reliance on the Father -- a divergence from the base gloss's neutral 'earnest seeking' toward a critiqued, faith-lacking mode of striving; the impact is to frame such seeking negatively relative to kingdom-seeking (implied contrast in the wider Matt.6/Luke.12 context).

5968.text: In Luke.12.30, no other M-code characteristic co-occurs alongside G1934 in the given role list; it stands as the sole home-cluster term, first pass over this verse.

5971.text: In Luke.12.30, 'seek after' is initiated by the nations of the world (party) directed toward 'these things' (material provisions, object), paralleling Matt.6.32's structure exactly.

6003.text: In Acts.12.19 'searched for' sits squarely within the base sense of earnest/directed seeking (Herod's manhunt for Peter) -- no notable divergence from the general stepGloss.

6006.text: Herod (party, G2264I) initiates the searching-operation, directed toward Peter (him, G0846) as the object sought, following his escape; this frames Herod as the seeking agent and Peter as the target.

6009.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs in Acts.12.19; the only home-cluster tag present belongs to this cluster's own M83 word. No M44 or other M-code characteristic is present in this verse to relate to.

6073.text: Luke.2.45 'searching for him' sits squarely within the base 'to seek, look for' sense (explicitly cited by the tree for Luke's usage of Jesus being sought), a plain physical search with no notable shift.

6083.text: In Luke.2.45 Joseph and Mary (implied party, 'they') initiate the searching, directed toward the boy Jesus (party, 'him') -- an operation of benevolent, anxious search for a lost family member.

6093.text: Luke.2.45: no other M-code characteristic co-occurs with the searching for the lost Jesus in this verse.

6258.text: In Rom.2.7 zeteo (kath' hupomonen ergou agathou doxan... zetousin) sits within its base gloss of diligent pursuit/striving toward a good end -- no unusual nuance beyond the standard 'seek/strive for' sense used elsewhere for pursuing eschatological goods.

6259.text: The operation word zeteo ('seek') is directed by 'those who' (the subject party, believers described by patient well-doing) toward the object 'glory and honor and immortality' -- the seeking party initiates the action toward the divine reward, not toward another person.

6260.text: Seeking (G2212) here functions as the operative disposition that yields glory (M22), honor (M71), and immortality (M61) via well-doing (M05) and patience (M34) and eternal life (M25); seeking is the pursuit-verb binding these other characteristics together as the sought objects/means, giving the first relational read of this verse's M-code cluster.

6352.text: In Prov.8.17 shachar sits within its base gloss of diligent/earnest seeking, matching its ordinary wisdom-literature use; no notable divergence from the term's general sense.

6353.text: The operation shachar ('seek diligently') is initiated by 'those who' (human seekers, the party) and directed toward Wisdom personified ('me'), paralleling the reciprocal 'love' verbs framing the verse.

6354.text: Shachar (diligent seeking) here operates alongside love (M51, ahav) as the twin verbs binding the human party to Wisdom; from shachar's vantage, it supplies the effortful, persistent dimension of the relationship that complements love's affective dimension, together yielding the promised finding -- first relational pass for this verse.

6372.text: In Isa 40.20 'seeks out' functions within the base gloss of seeking-to-secure (a craftsman), a straightforward practical-search sense with no notable added nuance.

6379.text: The impoverished man (implied party, 'he') initiates the seeking-operation, directed toward a skillful craftsman (party) to make an idol -- seeking here serves an idolatrous construction project.

6380.text: M64 (chooses, wood-selection), M16 (skillful), M23/M55 (setting up an idol) are present but describe separate stages of idol-making; seeking here specifically targets the craftsman, distinct from those other characteristics' own referents.

6438.text: In 1Sam.13.14 the Lord (T7/T10 party) is the initiator of seeking, directed toward finding 'a man after his own heart' as replacement ruler.

6448.text: In 1Sam.13.14 baqash co-occurs with M08/M74 (continue/keep) and M72 (kingdom) and M47 (heart); God's seeking-out of a new man is the counterpart to Saul's kingdom failing to continue and his failure to keep command -- a causal contrast rather than a shared characteristic-relation with baqash itself.

6549.text: In Job.10.6 and Ps.24.6 darash is used in its standard investigative/devotional senses (searching out sin; seeking God's face), with no notable divergence from the base gloss.

6553.text: In Job.10.6, baqash (seek out iniquity) and darash (search for sin, also M83) operate together as a synonymous parallel pair intensifying the single act of divine scrutiny; the two home-cluster terms mutually reinforce rather than each modifying a distinct outside M-code (M56 iniquity/sin are the objects, not characteristics being related to).

6554.text: In Job.10.6, darash (search for sin) pairs with baqash (seek out iniquity, also M83) as parallel intensifying synonyms describing the same divine investigative act; both terms jointly characterize the scrutiny rather than one qualifying the other externally.

6565.text: In Job.10.6, H1245 (seek) is an operation initiated by God ('you'), directed toward Job's iniquity as the object of scrutiny — God the initiator, Job's iniquity/sin the target.

6566.text: In Job.10.6, H1875 (search for) is an operation initiated by God, directed toward Job's sin — the same divine initiator/target pair as the parallel baqash clause.

6918.text: In Rom.3.11, Heb.11.6, and 1Pet.1.10 ekzeteo sits within its base sense of diligent/earnest seeking -- no notable divergence from the general gloss.

6920.text: Rom.3.11: ekzeteo ('seeks for God') is paired with understanding (M15, G4920, front-loaded) -- both are negated together, showing the seeking-characteristic and the understanding-characteristic as jointly absent in the indictment of universal sinfulness; seeking supplies the volitional/pursuit failure alongside understanding's cognitive failure.

6924.text: Rom.3.11: the (negated) seek-operation would be initiated by 'no one' (humanity as party) directed toward God (party); the negation asserts universal failure of the human party to initiate this operation.

7055.text: shachar's semantic range is narrower and more intensively focused than baqash or darash, concentrated almost entirely on 'diligent/early/earnest' seeking -- most frequently of God (Ps.63.1, Isa.26.9, Prov.8.17) but also of prey/food (Job.24.5) or a seductive target (Prov.7.15) -- its moral neutrality (like baqash's) is set by object, but its distinguishing feature vs. the other two Hebrew roots is the added connotation of urgency/priority tied etymologically to 'dawn'.

7056.text: G1567 (ekzeteo) and G1934 (epizeteo) both intensify the base zeteo root via a directional prefix (ek- 'out/thoroughly' vs epi- 'upon/toward'), and both share the same semantic split visible cross-strong: a devotional/diligent-seeking sense (ekzeteo: Acts.15.17, Heb.11.6, Rom.3.11, 1Pet.1.10; epizeteo: Heb.11.14, Heb.13.14, Acts.13.7) alongside a demanding/legal-exaction sense (ekzeteo: Luke.11.50-51, blood 'required'; epizeteo: Matt.12.39, Matt.16.4, Mark.8.12, Luke.11.29, demanding a sign; Acts.19.39, formal legal matter). Both Greek terms thus independently develop the same two-pole range (earnest seeking <-> exacting demand) from the same simple root, making them the closest pair in this subgroup.

7057.text: G1934 (epizeteo) shares with G1567 (ekzeteo) the same two-pole range: devotional/aspirational seeking (Heb.11.14 homeland, Heb.13.14 city to come, Rom.11.7 status Israel failed to obtain) versus demanding/exacting (Matt.12.39, Matt.16.4, Mark.8.12, Luke.11.29 demanding a sign; Acts.19.39 legal matter to be settled). Where ekzeteo's demand-sense is judicial/retributive (blood exacted), epizeteo's demand-sense is typically a testing or procedural request (a sign demanded from Jesus, a legal matter raised in assembly) -- a real difference in the character of what is 'demanded,' not merely a synonym overlap.

7058.text: H7836 (shachar) shares the subgroup's general 'intensive/earnest seeking' theme with G1567/G1934 conceptually (both Greek terms and shachar converge on devotional 'seek God/wisdom diligently' senses: shachar in Ps.63.1, Isa.26.9, Job.8.5, Prov.8.17, Ps.78.34 parallels ekzeteo in Acts.15.17/Heb.11.6/Rom.3.11 and epizeteo's aspirational uses), but there is no lexical or morphological relationship -- shachar is a distinct Hebrew root (tied etymologically to 'dawn/early') with no direct Greek cognate among this subgroup's members, and unlike ekzeteo/epizeteo it never carries a judicial 'demand an account/blood' sense; its 'demanding' pole (Job.7.21, God seeking Job) is ironic-reversal rather than legal exaction.

7059.text: Cross-strong, the two Greek members (ekzeteo, epizeteo) both attest a passive/legal-exaction voice pattern absent from shachar entirely: ekzeteo's future/aorist passive 'will be required/may be charged' (Luke.11.50-51) and epizeteo's passive-adjacent 'is matter of question/demand' senses in LSJ have no shachar counterpart -- shachar occurs only in Qal/Piel active-voice forms across all 12 occurrences, meaning the Hebrew member of this subgroup carries no attested passive 'held-to-account' construction, unlike its two Greek subgroup-mates.

7061.text: Epizeteo's four 'demanding a sign' occurrences (Matt.12.39, Matt.16.4, Mark.8.12, Luke.11.29) form a single tight cluster sharing one idiom -- 'this evil/adulterous generation seeks/demands a sign' -- functioning as a fixed Synoptic controversy formula rather than four independently-nuanced uses; this is the strong's own largest verse-grouping and is the clearest place where epizeteo's 'demand' sense (rather than its 'aspire/long for' sense) is activated.

7099.text: Isa.62.12's 'Sought Out' functions as a passive-participle EPITHET/name for the restored city rather than describing an active act of seeking performed by anyone in the verse -- a nominalized, identity-conferring nuance unique among this pass's occurrences, making darash itself the substance of a proper name/title.

7103.text: 1Chr.28.8's 'seek out' and Job.10.6's 'search for' both apply darash to an investigative-demand sense with a specific object -- commandments to be diligently observed versus iniquity being probed by God -- showing the same surface form covers both covenant-positive diligence and divine-forensic scrutiny.

7111.text: Where the subgroup's seeking is directed toward God/wisdom, it reveals a belief that the sought one exists, rewards, or can be found (Heb.11.6 'believe that he exists and that he rewards'; Prov.8.17 'those who seek me diligently find me'; Ps.63.1). Where it is directed toward a sign or an account (Matt.12.39/16.4, Luke.11.50-51), it reveals unbelief or a demand for proof/accountability rather than settled belief. In Heb.12.17 Esau's seeking reveals a late realization/perception that what was lost cannot be regained.

7113.text: Several occurrences orient the seeker toward a future fullness not yet possessed: Heb.11.14 and Heb.13.14 speak of seeking a homeland/city 'that is to come'; Isa.26.9 links earnest seeking to a future in which the world's inhabitants 'learn righteousness' when God's judgments come. This forward-orientation frames the seeking-characteristic as pilgrim/eschatological rather than merely present-satisfying.

7116.text: Both are attested. Reversible: seeking that leads to finding and repentance (Prov.8.17, Ps.78.34) can be entered into or renewed. Irreversible: Esau's seeking in Heb.12.17 comes after a disqualifying act and 'he found no chance to repent' -- the door once closed cannot be reopened by any degree of subsequent earnest seeking, making that particular instance of the characteristic irreversible in its outcome though not in the seeking-act itself.

7122.text: Yes. Ekzeteo/epizeteo's demanding sense operates through speech -- a spoken demand for a sign (Matt.12.39 'seeks for a sign', Mark.8.12, Luke.11.29) or a formally raised legal matter to be 'settled in the regular assembly' (Acts.19.39). Shachar's devotional sense in Hos.5.15/Job.8.5 pairs seeking with explicit speech-acts ('plead with the Almighty for mercy').

7125.text: In Rom.3.11 the person in whom seeking is characteristically absent is described as one who 'does not understand' -- an inner-being state of blindness/darkened understanding. In Heb.12.17 Esau, though he seeks with tears, is in a state of having 'found no chance to repent' -- the door is shut internally as well as circumstantially, so the seeking cannot take hold to produce repentance.

7135.text: The pattern shows the characteristic engaging soul/spirit level pervasively (Ps.63.1 'my soul thirsts,' Isa.26.9 'my spirit within me earnestly seeks') and occasionally the body as an expressive overflow (Ps.63.1 'my flesh faints'), but the body link is expressive/indicative rather than causally central -- the body registers the intensity of the soul/spirit's seeking rather than itself seeking. The characteristic never engages a purely bodily mechanism independent of soul/spirit direction.

7150.text: The structural opposite of intensive seeking is neglect or sparing -- explicitly named in Prov.13.24 as 'spares' (withholds effort/discipline), the negative pole set against 'diligent' in the same verse. More broadly, failure to seek (Rom.3.11's negated 'no one seeks') stands as the excluding condition: settled indifference or unbelief rather than active pursuit.

7153.text: Frequent co-occurring adjacent characteristics include: faith/belief (Heb.11.6, drawing near to God), understanding (Rom.3.11, paired negatively with seeking), love (Prov.8.17, Prov.13.24), repentance (Hos.5.15, Ps.78.34, Heb.12.17), guilt-acknowledgment (Hos.5.15), and hardening (Rom.11.7). Sign-demanding contexts co-occur with 'evil' and 'adulterous' descriptors of the generation (Matt.12.39, Matt.16.4, Luke.11.29).

7155.text: A recurring sequence: acknowledgment of guilt precedes seeking (Hos.5.15 'until they acknowledge their guilt and seek my face'); belief precedes seeking (Heb.11.6, 'must believe...and that he rewards those who seek him'); seeking precedes finding (Prov.8.17 'seek me diligently find me'); and being killed/judged precedes repentance which accompanies seeking (Ps.78.34 'When he killed them, they sought him; they repented').

7157.text: Yes -- seeking produces finding, by the mechanism of diligent, sustained pursuit meeting a responsive object: 'those who seek me diligently find me' (Prov.8.17). It can also produce learned righteousness at a corporate scale when paired with divine judgment (Isa.26.9, 'when your judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness').

7166.text: Across the verses, the characteristic follows a belief more often than it precedes one: Heb.11.6 makes belief in God's existence and rewarding character the explicit precondition for seeking; Hos.5.15 and Ps.78.34 show acknowledgment of guilt/repentance preceding the earnest seeking. In the demanding-sign occurrences, however, the seeking itself reveals an already-formed unbelieving judgment (the generation is 'evil and adulterous') rather than producing a new belief -- so the characteristic mostly follows or expresses prior belief/disposition rather than generating one, with the sign-demanding cases showing seeking as an expression of settled unbelief rather than a step toward belief.

7167.text: The subgroup shows clear future-fullness orientation: Heb.11.14 and Heb.13.14 (epizeteo) name a 'homeland' and 'city that is to come' not yet possessed; Acts.15.17 (ekzeteo) envisions Gentiles yet to seek the Lord eschatologically; Isa.26.9 (shachar) links earnest seeking to a future state when 'the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.' The movement is consistently toward something the person does not yet have -- a not-yet-attained relational or covenantal completeness.

7170.text: The evidence shows both: Esau's forfeiture in Heb.12.17 is irreversible (his tearful seeking cannot undo the prior choice, 'no chance to repent'), and Israel's failure in Rom.11.7 leads to hardening presented as a settled state ('the rest were hardened'). But other cases show seeking leading to attainment and reversal of separation (Prov.8.17 'find me'; Hos.5.15 leads to God's return). The transformation's reversibility depends entirely on timing and divine response, not on the intensity of the seeking itself.

7172.text: The evidence points to both created design and fallen distortion. The created-design pole appears where seeking God is the proper human posture (Heb.11.6, Ps.63.1, Prov.8.17, Acts.15.17) -- an intended capacity oriented toward God as its fulfillment. The fallen-condition pole appears where seeking is either absent altogether (Rom.3.11, 'no one seeks for God') or twisted into hostile demand (Matt.16.4, testing sign-seeking) or exacted judicially against guilt (Luke.11.50-51). The same capacity for intensive seeking is thus shown as originally God-directed but corruptible into either default neglect or adversarial demand.

7173.text: In devotional occurrences the felt quality is intense and bodily: Ps.63.1 pairs 'earnestly I seek' with 'my soul thirsts... my flesh faints,' and Isa.26.9 pairs it with 'my soul yearns... in the night.' These are not settled dispositions alone but acute, felt longing, expressed through explicit bodily/emotional language (thirst, fainting, yearning at night).

7180.text: The characteristic is blocked or fruitless under conditions of unbelief (Rom.3.11, 'no one seeks for God' as part of a universal indictment of sinfulness), of prior settled disqualification (Heb.12.17, Esau finds 'no chance to repent' though he sought with tears), of hostile testing rather than genuine inquiry (Matt.12.39/16.4, an 'evil and adulterous generation' demands a sign), and of persistent unresponsiveness to prior calls (Prov.1.28, wisdom's earlier call refused, so later diligent seeking finds no answer). No adversarial-spirit interference is shown in any occurrence; blockage arises from the seeker's own unbelief, prior refusal, or a closed opportunity, not from another spirit's distortion.

7184.text: The relational scope is universal in principle (Rom.3.11's indictment applies to 'no one' -- all humanity; Acts.15.17 explicitly includes Gentiles) but realized unevenly: the elect obtain what is sought while 'the rest' do not (Rom.11.7), and the sign-demanding generation is characterized as excluded from the category of genuine seekers by its own 'evil and adulterous' disposition (Matt.12.39). Inclusion is thus universal in offer but differentiated in outcome by faith/unbelief.

7185.text: Assessing what the pattern of presence/absence of this characteristic across the human person indicates for its place in the divine image would require comparing against the cluster's science-extract or broader image-of-God data not carried in this subgroup's own occurrence evidence; flagging needs_adjacent_verse_context because determining the D5.1.1 presence/absence pattern itself depends on data outside this subgroup's verses.

7187.text: The human-to-God direction shows a relationship of dependent trust and reward-expectation, not self-sufficiency: the person who seeks believes God exists, rewards seekers (Heb.11.6), and can be found by diligent seekers (Prov.8.17, Jer-style promise pattern) -- the relationship is one where God is approachable and responsive to genuine seeking, contrasted starkly with Rom.3.11's indictment that fallen humanity does not by default seek God at all.

7190.text: Where the characteristic is present as genuine, faith-grounded pursuit of God (Heb.11.6, Ps.63.1), it indicates the divine image functioning rightly in its relational orientation toward God. Where it is absent entirely (Rom.3.11, universal indictment) it indicates the divine image's relational faculty toward God is disabled/inoperative in fallen humanity apart from grace. Where it is present but distorted into hostile demand (Matt.16.4) it indicates the image's capacity for genuine relational reaching has been turned toward self-justifying testing instead.

7191.text: The evidence engages spirit/soul-level seats primarily (Ps.63.1: 'my soul thirsts'; Isa.26.9: 'my spirit within me earnestly seeks') with body given expressive rather than causal role ('my flesh faints for you' as an outward sign of the soul's longing, not a bodily-originated act). The judicial/demand occurrences (Luke.11.50-51, Matt.16.4) engage no inner-constitutional level explicitly, operating instead at the level of corporate/legal accountability. The body link where present is expressive/indicative -- signaling the intensity of soul-level longing -- never the seat or origin of the seeking itself.

7193.text: The evidence shows movement primarily spirit/soul-to-behavior (inward longing producing the outward act of seeking, Isa.26.9, Ps.63.1) and, distinctly, movement onto the person from an external source in the judicial occurrences -- God's demand/requirement is imposed externally upon 'this generation' (Luke.11.50-51) rather than arising from within the person. No angelic or adversarial-spirit movement is attested anywhere in this subgroup's evidence.

7195.text: God's extension of reward/response to seekers shows a disposition of genuine responsiveness and reward-giving rather than aloofness: he 'rewards those who seek him' (Heb.11.6) and promises 'find me' to diligent seekers (Prov.8.17), and his withdrawal in Hos.5.15 is itself framed as purposeful, aimed at provoking the very seeking that will restore relationship -- disciplinary rather than punitive abandonment.

7196.text: In Prov.8.17, personified Wisdom's genuine extension of herself to seekers is accompanied by her own prior orientation of love toward them ('I love those who love me') -- reciprocal affection precedes and accompanies her being found, showing the giver's inner condition is one of settled favor toward the seeker, not indifference.

7200.text: The evidence shows no adversarial-spirit activity attached to the characteristic itself; the sign-demanding occurrences locate the corrupting force in the human generation's own moral condition ('evil and adulterous') rather than in any depicted spirit's interference, so this subgroup's occurrences do not evidence the characteristic as a site of adversarial spiritual activity.

7203.text: The characteristic consistently engages volitional and affective faculties (will/desire: Ps.63.1's thirst, Prov.8.17's love-paired diligence) and occasionally cognitive faculties (belief, Heb.11.6's 'must believe'), but rarely engages purely rational/discursive faculties in isolation -- even the 'searched and inquired carefully' of 1Pet.1.10 (investigative diligence) is paired with prophetic revelation rather than autonomous reasoning. This pattern indicates the characteristic's nature is fundamentally an act of the whole person's directed will and desire toward an object, not a purely intellectual exercise.

7204.text: The characteristic is primarily an ACT -- an enacted operation of intensive seeking or demanding, attested grammatically almost exclusively as verbs (active, passive, participial) across all three member strongs, rather than as a noun-form disposition, condition, or quality. Where it recurs habitually (e.g. Heb.13.14's ongoing pilgrim-seeking, or 'this generation' repeatedly demanding a sign) it functions as a repeated act rather than a distinct static disposition-noun.

7206.text: The structural opposite of intensive/exhaustive seeking is settled neglect or non-seeking -- most explicitly Rom.3.11's negated form, 'no one seeks for God,' which stands as the direct grammatical and conceptual antonym: not casual disinterest but a total absence of the pursuit the characteristic names. Complacent self-sufficiency (needing no rewarder, requiring no restoration) is the inner-being reality that excludes it.

7207.text: The characteristic excludes/resists casual or half-hearted inquiry at its edge -- its intensifying prefixes/root explicitly mark it off from a merely passing glance or occasional interest (zeteo's plain form); it also resists premature closure, refusing to settle for partial or token search (Prov.1.28's failed 'diligent' seeking shows the characteristic still names genuine effort even when unsuccessful, distinguishing it from giving up).

7208.text: The characteristic ends where finding/obtaining begins -- it is not the possession of the object but the reaching toward it (Prov.8.17's 'seek me diligently find me' shows seeking as the antecedent act distinct from finding, the consequent state); it is also distinct from mere calling/asking (a single request) since it implies sustained, thorough effort rather than a single utterance, and distinct from settled belief/perception (M0.1.1's judgement-content) since it is the pursuit that may precede, follow, or accompany belief rather than being identical with it.

7209.text: Adjacent characteristics recur across the subgroup's verses: faith/belief (Heb.11.6, pistis-family), understanding (Rom.3.11, paired negation with G4920), grace/salvation (1Pet.1.10), repentance (Heb.12.17, Hos.5.15, Ps.78.34), love (Prov.8.17, Prov.13.24), guilt-acknowledgment (Hos.5.15), and hardening (Rom.11.7). Faith/belief and repentance are the most frequent co-occurring characteristics, appearing across multiple member strongs.

7211.text: A recurring sequence: acknowledgment of guilt/distress precedes earnest seeking (Hos.5.15: 'until they acknowledge their guilt and seek my face'); repentance accompanies or closely follows seeking (Ps.78.34: 'they repented and sought God earnestly'); and seeking precedes finding (Prov.8.17: 'those who seek me diligently find me'). The consistent order is: acknowledgment/distress -> seeking -> repentance/finding.

7212.text: The sequence is developmental and causal rather than merely correlational: acknowledgment of guilt causally opens the way for seeking (Hos.5.15's 'until'), and seeking causally produces finding (Prov.8.17's promise), showing a real chain of cause-and-effect rather than accidental co-occurrence -- though the chain can be broken (Prov.1.28's failed seeking shows the causal chain is conditioned on timing/prior response, not automatic).

7213.text: Yes -- the characteristic produces finding/attainment as its natural fruit by the mechanism of sustained, thorough pursuit meeting a responsive object: 'those who seek me diligently find me' (Prov.8.17); it also produces reward from God as its fruit (Heb.11.6, 'he rewards those who seek him'), by the mechanism of divine responsiveness to genuine faith-grounded pursuit.

He *"burned with anger at Job because he justified himself rather than God"*, and at the friends *"because they had found no answer, although they had declared Job to be in the wrong"* (32:2–3).; He calls the listeners to weigh Job's case together, and calls that weighing a choosing: *"Hear my words, you wise men"* … *"for the ear tests words as the palate tastes food"*; *"Let us choose what is right; let us know among ourselves what is good"* (v2–4). The choosing here is not of a course of life. It is a judgement: picking out what is right in the case before them.; The picture is tasting. The ear tests (H0974) as the palate tastes (H2938). Then *"let us know among ourselves what is good"* uses the same words as Barzillai's *"Can I discern what is pleasant and what is not"* (2Sa 19:35): know (H3045), between (H0996), good (H2896). Barzillai said the palate's knowing had gone with age. Elihu uses the palate as the picture for weighing words.; What they are to weigh is Job's own claim. Elihu quotes it: *"I am in the right, and God has taken away my right"* (v5). He judges it at once: *"What man is like Job, who drinks up scoffing like water"*, *"who travels in company with evildoers"* (v7–8). His ground is God's justice: *"far be it from God that he should do wickedness"* (v10); *"his eyes are on the ways of a man, and he sees all his steps"* (v21).

20306.text: What this verse shows of choosing, as weighed by another: Weighing another person's choices is itself a choosing, *"what is right"*.; It is made together (*"let us … among ourselves"*), by testing words as the palate tests food.; It is a judgement on a case, not a course of life.; The one who calls for it has already decided (v7–8).

20394.text: Isaiah 10:7: "But he does not so intend, and his heart does not so think": > Q1 citation: ✅ Accurate. 10.13 quotes vv5 and 7 in *Those who carry it out* ("Assyria is the rod, and has its own heart") and points to v7 in *What changes it*. Accurate. (v1 said 10.13 gives only a pointer. That was wrong; see corrections.); >; > Q2 M64: Include: corroborates and adds. Corroborates 10.13: the one God uses has his own heart. New, for 10.4 and 10.7: the arrogant heart that boasts "By the strength of my hand I have done it" is punished (vv12–15).; >; > Q3 other M-codes: M10 destroy: carried in 10.13. In the passage, the arrogant heart (v12): a pointer for pride when it is taken up.; Assyria is *"the rod of my anger"* (v5), sent against a godless nation (v6). *"But he does not so intend, and his heart does not so think; but it is in his heart to destroy"* (v7).; He boasts: *"By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom"* (v13). The Lord *"will punish the speech of the arrogant heart of the king of Assyria"* (v12). *"Shall the axe boast over him who hews with it?"* (v15).; "Think" is H2803I.

20516.text:
What the heart says is mostly a verdict: about God's seeing, about self, about the future. Kinds seen:
• denial that God sees (Ps 10:11, 13; Zep 1:12; Isa 47:10)
• self-exaltation (Isa 14:13; 47:8; Zep 2:15; Obd 3; Eze 28:2)
• self-credit (Deu 8:17; 9:4)
• fear (Deu 7:17; 1Sa 27:1)
• enquiry (Ecc 1:16; 2:1, 15; 3:17–18; Deu 18:21; Jer 13:22)
• denial of God (Ps 14:1; 53:1)

20522.text: Love reckons as God reckons: love is "not resentful" (does not count wrong), as God is "not counting their trespasses"; "may it not be charged against them"

21301.text: Call is a purposeful act of the inner being turned to God: calling or crying out to the Lord, or on his name, in need, trust, praise or worship, or refusing to.

21311.text: Called here only names, designates or labels a person, place or thing (to be called such a name, to call it so); no inner-being operation is voiced by it.

21322.text: Calling is here the outward act of summoning, addressing or sending for another person or thing; it bears on the other's response but names no inner-being operation of the one who calls.

21434.text: Wrath is here the anger, wrath or fury of God against persons or nations (kindled, poured out, turned away, executed, provoked); it is God's own act upon them, and bears on their inner response, which other words of the verse name, if at all.

21460.text: Holy is here the standing of those set apart for God (the holy people, the saints, a holy nation); it names what the person is brought into, not an inner operation of its own.

21477.text: Righteousness is here the godliness, devoutness, reverence or uprightness of a person as a state of the heart toward God or toward what is right (a devout man who feared God, godliness trained and pursued, uprightness of heart, reverence and awe).

21519.text: Chooses is here a person's own act of choosing or deciding: a purposeful act of the will that picks one thing, way, person or course over another (choose life, choose whom you will serve, decided in his heart, Mary has chosen the good portion).

21546.text: Arise here is bodily rising, going or acting, or something coming into being, or God arising; no human inner-being operation is qualified.

21639.text: Play here is playing an instrument, playing with animals, or the revelry after a feast; no inner-being operation is named or qualified.

21709.text: Walk here is bodily walking, or the course of conduct (walk in his ways, statutes or customs); the walk itself is outward conduct, no inner-being operation is named or qualified in it.

21719.text: Well-doing is where patience is exercised: patience in well-doing, seeking glory and honor and immortality.

21732.text: Young here is youth in age, a young man, woman, animal or offspring; a description of age or kind, no inner-being operation is named or qualified.

21733.text: 'find' here only names a physical search or finding, a practical or judicial finding, a record search or reconnaissance; no inner-being operation is voiced by it.

21735.text: 'find' is here the finding of a person as the end of seeking (the Lord, wisdom); it names the outcome of the seeking, with the person as the relational target.

21759.text: 'seek' is here the outward search or pursuit through which a purpose is carried out (a hunt for a person, God's search for the lost or for sin, the neglect of such a search); it is the outward act, and the inner intent or care is named by other words or only implied.
